# OpenCode V2 Skill Mechanics

How OpenCode V2 discovers, advertises, and loads skills, and where its behavior
diverges from Claude Code when the same skill directories are shared.

> Authoritative reference: <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills>. The Claude Code
> side of the contrast is in [claude-code/skills.md](../claude-code/skills.md).

## Discovery locations

OpenCode searches a fixed set of roots automatically. Project-scoped roots are
resolved by walking from the current directory up to the project root, so a
skill placed at any intermediate level is found.

| Scope | Root | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Global | `~/.config/opencode/skills` | Native location |
| Global (compatibility) | `~/.claude/skills` | Read in place; no import step |
| Global (compatibility) | `~/.agents/skills` | Read in place |
| Project | `.opencode/skills` | Native location |
| Project (compatibility) | `.claude/skills` | Read in place |
| Project (compatibility) | `.agents/skills` | Read in place |
| Config | `skills` array | Additional sources, highest precedence |

`~/.codex/skills` is **not** an automatic location. A Codex installation's skills
are invisible unless that path is added to the `skills` config array.

The compatibility roots are a discovery convenience only. They change where
files are read from, not how the content is interpreted — see
[No `!` injection](#no--injection).

## Skill forms and IDs

Two layouts each count as exactly one skill:

1. A root-level `*.md` file.
2. A directory containing `SKILL.md`.

Walk-time exclusions: hidden files and directories, `node_modules`, and any
nesting deeper than six levels. A skill buried seven levels down is not
discovered.

The skill ID is derived from the **path**, not from the frontmatter `name`.
The ID is case-sensitive, and the frontmatter `name` does not override it. Two
skills whose `name` fields match but whose paths differ are distinct skills;
renaming the directory changes the ID and therefore changes every reference to
it, including permission rules.

## Precedence

Later-registered sources win on duplicate IDs. Registration order, lowest to
highest:

1. Built-in skills
2. `.claude/skills`
3. `.agents/skills`
4. `~/.config/opencode/skills`
5. Project `.opencode/skills`
6. Explicit `skills` config entries

The ordering is per-ID, not per-source: a duplicate ID in a higher layer shadows
only that ID, and every other skill from the lower layer remains available.

## Skills are not slash commands

Skill invocation and slash commands are separate mechanisms that do not
overlap.

At each model step, OpenCode advertises the permitted skills to the model by
**ID, name, and description only**. The body is not in context. The model loads
a skill by calling the `skill` tool; a user loads one by mentioning `@skill-id`.

Slash commands are defined under `commands/` or the `commands` config key. A
skill never appears in the command palette on its own. A workflow that must be
one keystroke away needs a command definition that points at the skill, not just
the skill.

## No `!` injection

This is the sharpest divergence from Claude Code.

Claude Code expands `!`-prefixed command blocks inside skill content **before**
the model sees it, substituting command output inline. OpenCode does not perform
this expansion. The literal backtick-command text is delivered to the model
unrendered.

Consequences for a skill written for Claude Code:

1. Every injected value is silently lost. Nothing errors; the model receives the
   command string where the output should be.
2. The model must be instructed to run those commands itself with its own tools,
   which costs a tool round trip per injection and makes the result dependent on
   what the model chooses to execute.
3. Frontmatter is not a lever here. The behavior is in the loader, not the skill.

Observed directly on a skill whose body contained injection blocks: the loaded
body showed the commands rather than their output.

## Gating and visibility

The `skill` permission action takes the skill ID as its resource.

| Action | Advertised to model | Loadable |
|--------|--------------------|----------|
| `allow` | Yes | Yes |
| `ask` | Yes, with a prompt before loading | Yes |
| `deny` | No | Rejected |

Because the resource is the ID, a `deny` rule must match the path-derived ID, not
the frontmatter `name`.

Separately from permissions, a skill can be hidden from the model's advertised
list while staying loadable by explicit ID:

- `metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: false`
- `disable-model-invocation: true`

Both leave the skill reachable by `@skill-id` and by an explicit `skill` tool
call. This is the correct setting for a skill that should only run when a user
asks for it, as opposed to one that must never run (`deny`).

## Portability frontmatter is accepted but not enforced

V2 accepts portability-oriented frontmatter such as `license` and
`compatibility` and does not interpret it. The same holds for the recommended ID
constraints:

| Recommendation | Enforced by V2 |
|----------------|----------------|
| Kebab-case ID | No |
| ID length 1-64 characters | No |
| `name` matches directory | No |
| `license` / `compatibility` semantics | No |

A non-conforming ID is accepted at load time. Nothing in the loader reports it,
so validation is the author's responsibility. Any reference to the skill —
permission rules, `@mention` strings, command definitions — must use the
path-derived ID.
